g) Members of the public, only when visiting the Port Area for an approved purpose, such as attendance at a scheduled meeting, official inquiry, or guided tour.

**9. COMPLIANCE MONITORING**

**9.1 General Obligation**

All licensees, permit holders, terminal operators, shipping lines, agents, and service providers operating within the jurisdiction of the Lagos Port Authority shall comply with the provisions of this Directive, the Lagos Port Authority Act, and all subsidiary legislation, guidelines, and circulars issued by the Authority from time to time.

Compliance with this Directive does not relieve any person or entity of the obligation to comply with the requirements of other applicable laws and regulations, including those administered by the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA), the Nigeria Customs Service, the Nigerian Ports Authority, and other relevant agencies of the Federal Government.

**9.2 Monitoring Mechanisms**

The Authority shall monitor compliance with this Directive through the following mechanisms:

(a) **Inspections** – Authorised officers of the Authority may, at any reasonable time, enter upon any terminal, berth, warehouse, or other facility within the port limits, and inspect any vessel, equipment, cargo, document, or record, for the purpose of verifying compliance with this Directive.

(b) **Audits** – The Authority may conduct periodic or risk-based audits of the financial records, operational procedures, and safety management systems of terminal operators and other regulated persons.

(c) **Electronic Surveillance** – The Authority shall utilise its Vessel Traffic Management Information System (VTMIS), CCTV infrastructure, and other electronic monitoring tools to track vessel movements, berth occupancy, and cargo operations.

(d) **Documentary Review** – The Authority may require the production of any document, record, or information reasonably necessary to ascertain compliance, including manifests, stowage plans, crew lists, gate passes, and equipment maintenance logs.

(e) **Port State Control** – The Authority shall coordinate with NIMASA and other relevant agencies in the conduct of port state control inspections and examinations.

**9.3 Obligation to Cooperate**

Every person to whom this Directive applies shall:

(a) afford all reasonable facilities and assistance to authorised officers conducting inspections or audits;

(b) answer truthfully any question put by an authorised officer in the course of an inspection or audit;

(c) produce, upon demand, any document or record required for the purpose of verifying compliance; and

(d) permit the taking of photographs, samples, measurements, or other evidence reasonably required.

Failure or refusal to cooperate with an authorised officer shall constitute a breach of this Directive and shall be treated as a separate and distinct contravention.

**9.4 Record-Keeping Obligations**

Terminal operators, shipping lines, agents, and other regulated persons shall maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all operations subject to this Directive, including:

(a) vessel arrival and departure times;

(b) berth allocation and utilisation records;

(c) cargo handling tallies and damage reports;

(d) equipment maintenance and inspection logs;

(e) crew and visitor access registers;

(f) security incident reports;

(g) environmental monitoring data; and

(h) all invoices, receipts, and payment records relating to charges and fees.

Such records shall be retained for a period of not less than five (5) years from the date of the transaction or event to which they relate, and shall be made available to the Authority upon request.

**9.5 Self-Reporting of Incidents**

Any person who becomes aware of an incident, accident, or irregularity that may constitute a breach of this Directive, or that may compromise the safety, security, or environmental integrity of the port, shall report the matter to the Authority within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming so aware. Reports may be made through the Authority’s designated email address or through the Port Control Centre.

| **C** | Lowest | All other vessels, including but not limited to: vessels awaiting survey or repair; laid-up vessels; vessels calling for crew changes or stores only; and vessels with unresolved documentation or compliance issues. |

3.3 Assignment to a priority class shall be made by the Scheduling Office upon receipt of a completed Berth Request Form (Form BSF-01). The assignment shall be confirmed in writing to the Vessel Agent within one (1) Working Day of receipt of the completed form.

3.4 A vessel may be reclassified from one class to another where there is a material change in circumstances. Reclassification shall be at the discretion of the Scheduling Office and shall be communicated in writing.

**4.0 CRITERIA FOR CLASS A ASSIGNMENT**

4.1 In addition to the categories of cargo listed in Table 1, the following factors shall be taken into account when considering assignment to Class A:

a) The vessel's compliance with the LPA's Vessel Arrival Notification requirements, including submission of the Notice of Readiness and the Pre-Arrival Security Information within the stipulated timeframes;

c) The nature and urgency of the cargo, supported by documentary evidence such as a Bill of Lading, a letter from the consignee, or a directive from a relevant Federal Ministry or Agency;

d) The vessel's overall safety and environmental compliance record; and

e) Any other factor that the Scheduling Office considers relevant to the efficient and safe operation of the port.

4.2 By way of example, the following vessels may be considered for Class A assignment:

a) A tanker carrying aviation fuel for the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, where the fuel supply is below the minimum operating threshold;

b) A container vessel on a fixed weekly schedule operated by a line with a consistent record of on-time arrival and departure, such as Delta Shipping Lines. c) A vessel carrying food items such as rice or wheat consigned to the National Food Reserve Agency; and

**6. COMMUNICATION AND REPORTING PROTOCOLS**

6.1 All communications between vessels, agents, terminal operators, and the Authority shall be conducted through the designated VHF channels as listed in the current edition of the Lagos Port Complex Information Booklet. The primary working channel for berthing operations is VHF Channel 12. The pilot boarding station shall monitor VHF Channel 16 continuously during daylight hours and when a pilot is embarked.

6.2 The Authority shall maintain a 24-hour Harbour Control Room. The Control Room may be contacted on telephone +234 (0) 1 463 9000, extension 4501, or by email at harbourcontrol@lagosport.gov.ng. Urgent matters concerning navigational safety, pollution incidents, or security breaches shall be reported immediately to the Control Room, followed by written confirmation within two (2) hours.

6.3 Agents shall submit the following documents to the Harbour Master's office not later than twenty-four (24) hours before the estimated time of arrival of any vessel:

(a) Notice of Readiness;
(b) Crew and passenger list;
(c) Last port of call certificate;
(d) Cargo manifest summary;
(e) Certificate of ship's registry;
(f) International Tonnage Certificate, where applicable.

6.4 Any change to the estimated time of arrival, estimated time of departure, or berthing requirements shall be communicated to the Control Room and the relevant terminal operator without delay. Where a vessel is delayed by more than six (6) hours, the agent shall submit a revised notice.

6.5 The Authority publishes a Daily Berth Allocation List. This list shall be issued at 16:00 hours each day and shall reflect the planned berthing sequence for the following day. The list shall be made available on the LPA notice board, the official website, and through the electronic data interchange system. Terminal operators and agents shall confirm receipt of the list by 18:00 hours.

6.6 The Authority shall hold a quarterly stakeholder meeting to review port performance, discuss operational challenges, and coordinate planned maintenance or dredging activities. The meeting shall be held on the third Thursday of the months of March, June, September, and December, commencing at 10:00 hours in the LPA Conference Hall. All terminal operators, shipping line representatives, and licensed agents are expected to attend or send a representative with authority to make commitments on their behalf.

6.7 The Authority may issue operational advisories or circulars at any time. These communications shall be numbered sequentially within the calendar year and shall be binding on all port users from the date and time of issue, unless otherwise stated.

---

**7. SAFETY REQUIREMENTS**

7.1 All persons entering the port operational area shall wear appropriate personal protective equipment, including a hard hat, high-visibility vest, and safety footwear. Failure to comply shall result in the person being denied access or removed from the operational area.

7.2 No person shall enter a restricted area without the appropriate security clearance and a valid purpose for being there. Restricted areas include, but are not limited to, the container freight station, the bonded warehouse zone, the fuel storage area, and the berths designated for the handling of dangerous goods.

7.3 Smoking, the use of naked flames, and the operation of non-certified electrical equipment are prohibited within twenty-five (25) metres of any vessel alongside, any cargo in transit, or any storage facility containing flammable materials.

documents.title: Lagos Port Authority Operations Directive 2024-07
documents.content:
**9. COMPLIANCE MONITORING**

**9.1 General Obligation**

All licensees, permit holders, terminal operators, shipping lines, agents, and service providers operating within the jurisdiction of the Lagos Port Authority shall comply with the provisions of this Directive, the Lagos Port Authority Act, and all subsidiary legislation, guidelines, and circulars issued by the Authority from time to time.

Compliance with this Directive does not relieve any person or entity of the obligation to comply with the requirements of other applicable laws and regulations, including those administered by the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA), the Nigeria Customs Service, the Nigerian Ports Authority, and other relevant agencies of the Federal Government.

**9.2 Monitoring Mechanisms**

The Authority shall monitor compliance with this Directive through the following mechanisms:

(a) **Inspections** – Authorised officers of the Authority may, at any reasonable time, enter upon any terminal, berth, warehouse, or other facility within the port limits, and inspect any vessel, equipment, cargo, document, or record, for the purpose of verifying compliance with this Directive.

(b) **Audits** – The Authority may conduct periodic or risk-based audits of the financial records, operational procedures, and safety management systems of terminal operators and other regulated persons.

(c) **Electronic Surveillance** – The Authority shall utilise its Vessel Traffic Management Information System (VTMIS), CCTV infrastructure, and other electronic monitoring tools to track vessel movements, berth occupancy, and cargo operations.

(d) **Documentary Review** – The Authority may require the production of any document, record, or information reasonably necessary to ascertain compliance, including manifests, stowage plans, crew lists, gate passes, and equipment maintenance logs.

(e) **Port State Control** – The Authority shall coordinate with NIMASA and other relevant agencies in the conduct of port state control inspections and examinations.

**9.3 Obligation to Cooperate**

Every person to whom this Directive applies shall:

(a) afford all reasonable facilities and assistance to authorised officers conducting inspections or audits;

(b) answer truthfully any question put by an authorised officer in the course of an inspection or audit;

(c) produce, upon demand, any document or record required for the purpose of verifying compliance; and

(d) permit the taking of photographs, samples, measurements, or other evidence reasonably required.

Failure or refusal to cooperate with an authorised officer shall constitute a breach of this Directive and shall be treated as a separate and distinct contravention.

**9.4 Record-Keeping Obligations**

Terminal operators, shipping lines, agents, and other regulated persons shall maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all operations subject to this Directive, including:

(a) vessel arrival and departure times;

(b) berth allocation and utilisation records;

(c) cargo handling tallies and damage reports;

(d) equipment maintenance and inspection logs;

(e) crew and visitor access registers;

(f) security incident reports;

(g) environmental monitoring data; and

(h) all invoices, receipts, and payment records relating to charges and fees.

Such records shall be retained for a period of not less than five (5) years from the date of the transaction or event to which they relate, and shall be made available to the Authority upon request.

**9.5 Self-Reporting of Incidents**

Any person who becomes aware of an incident, accident, or irregularity that may constitute a breach of this Directive, or that may compromise the safety, security, or environmental integrity of the port, shall report the matter to the Authority within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming so aware. Reports may be made through the Authority’s designated email address or through the Port Control Centre.

The quarantine status of MV Atlantic Trader is clear. This confirmation was obtained from the Port Health Services duty officer, Dr. Ngozi Eze, at 08:50 on the day of inspection, and the corresponding PHS clearance form (PHS/LAG/2024/1187) was sighted by the inspecting team at the boarding station.

5.2 Maritime Declaration of Health

The Maritime Declaration of Health (MDH) was submitted by the Master, Capt. Petros Stavrou, upon arrival. The declaration was reviewed and found to be consistent with the crew list and the ship's medical log. The MDH stated that there were no cases of illness on board during the last 15 days, no deaths among crew or passengers, and no reason to suspect any infectious disease on board.

The ship's medical log was examined for the period 2024-03-01 to 2024-03-15. Entries indicate one case of mild gastroenteritis among crew (reported 2024-03-08), which resolved without medical intervention. No other notable medical entries were recorded.

5.3 Crew Health and Vaccination Records

Crew vaccination records were reviewed for yellow fever, as required for vessels arriving from West African ports. All 22 crew members have valid yellow fever vaccination certificates. The most recent certificate was issued to the 3rd Engineer, Mr. Rajesh Kumar, on 2023-02-14, valid through 2024-02-14, and renewed on 2024-02-10 (valid through 2034-02-10). All other crew certificates were confirmed valid.

No requirement for malaria prophylaxis was noted in the crew medical records, and no standing instruction from PHS was in effect for this vessel.

5.4 Vessel Sanitation and Pest Control

Port Health Services vessel_quarantine_status is clear. Record status: current.

The vessel's sanitation conditions were inspected in the following areas:

- Galley and food storage: Satisfactory. Temperature logs for refrigerated stores were current and within acceptable range (2°C – 4°C for chilled, -18°C for frozen). No evidence of pest infestation observed.
- Crew accommodation: Satisfactory. Cabins were clean and well-ventilated. No standing water or signs of rodent activity.
- Hospital and medical stores: Satisfactory. Medical chest contents were checked against the WHO/ILO/IMO Medical First Aid Guide recommendations. Expiry dates of critical items (IV fluids, analgesics, antibiotics) were verified and are all valid beyond 2024-09-30.
- Potable water system: Satisfactory. Chlorine residual test was conducted on potable water tanks, showing 0.5 ppm free chlorine. Water samples were taken for laboratory analysis in accordance with PHS requirements.

5.5 Garbage and Waste Disposal

Garbage management plan was reviewed and found to be in compliance. The vessel's garbage record book was examined; entries were up to date as of 2024-03-14. No incinerator on board; waste is landed at port reception facilities. Prior port of call (Tema) garbage receipt was sighted, dated 2024-03-12.

Sewage holding tank capacity: 12.4 m³. The vessel is fitted with a sewage treatment plant (Type II, certified by Bureau Veritas). The treatment plant was tested during the inspection; discharge effluent sample showed no visible suspended solids and no odour.

5.6 Ballast Water Management

Ballast water management plan and record book were reviewed. The vessel is fitted with a ballast water treatment system (UV + filtration, model BWTS-500, manufactured by OceanGuard, installed 2020). The system was in operation during the voyage from Tema. Ballast water exchange was not required as the system is IMO D-2 compliant.

Ballast water record book entries were verified and found to be consistent with the ship's voyage data. Total ballast water on board at time of inspection: 8,200 MT. No uptake of ballast water was conducted in Nigerian waters.
